title: Jonah and the Oath
premise: Ines Almeida, a mercenary oathbound to the silent god Veth, has spent years running contraband through the Thornfell mountains while their god's silence deepens into shame. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark, Ines discovers the truth: Veth did not abandon them — the god's soul was sold to the Undercourt beneath Thornfell, and every oath sworn in its name is now a leash held by the court's regent, Lady Sable. To free Veth, Ines must steal the soul back before the new moon seals the court for a century, aided by a disgraced ward-keeper, a debt-bound smuggler rival, and a child who remembers being a god. At the climax Ines learns their own memories were the payment that bought Veth's capture, and they must choose between restoring their forgotten past or shattering the oath to save everyone bound by it; they break the oath, unmaking their loyalty to free the god, and walk out of the mountain remembering nothing but choosing it anyway.
about_author: D. M. Montrose is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction about the things that live under them. They write in a cabin at the edge of a forest that locals refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Salt Road Contract
chapters.summary: Ines Almeida's POV. Ines runs one last smuggling job through Thornfell for coin to pay off their oath-tithe to the silent god Veth, guided by muscle memory of roads they can't explain knowing. A toll-keeper mentions the wards flickering. The beat is uneasy competence masking dread.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: Ward-keeper Odile Ferran's POV. Odile discovers the mountain wards were not keeping smugglers out but something in — and someone inside has been feeding them lies for years. She burns her records and flees as the first star goes dark. Beat: institutional betrayal and cold fear.

chapters.title: Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Every star vanishes at once mid-crossing; the wards fall like glass. Ines's oath-brand flares, dragging them toward the mountain against their will. They rescue a lost child, Wren, from the rockfall. Beat: awe curdling into compulsion.

chapters.title: The Debt-Bound
chapters.summary: Rival smuggler Cassian Vole's POV. Cassian is summoned by Lady Sable's agents and ordered to hunt Ines, his old partner, in exchange for erasing his family's debt. He accepts and hates himself. Beat: resentment sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Wren Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Wren speaks in Veth's cadence and knows Ines's real name — one Ines doesn't recognize. The child claims to be a fragment of the god's memory, hidden in mortal flesh. Beat: vertigo of identity, tenderness toward the strange child.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, crossing paths with Ines. Odile reveals the Wardens' founding bargain: Veth traded its soul for the mountain's protection, then tried to take it back. She carries the only map to the Undercourt's door. Beat: guilt offered as alliance.

chapters.title: Cassian Catches Up
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Cassian ambushes them at the flooded pass; old loyalty makes the fight half-hearted on both sides. Ines spares him and shows him Wren, whose presence cracks his certainty. Beat: violence interrupted by grief.

chapters.title: The Tithe Houses
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Cassian reports falsely to Sable's agents, buying time, and sees the tithe houses where oath-sworn mercenaries are drained to feed the captive god-soul. He understands what his own brand means. Beat: horror of complicity.

chapters.title: Down the Hollow Ways
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The four descend through the hollow ways, where Ines's smuggler knowledge becomes uncanny — these roads were built for gods, and Ines's body remembers why. Wren grows weaker as they near the court. Beat: wonder shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. First sight of the Undercourt: a mirrored city lit by stolen starlight, its nobles wearing faces harvested from the oath-sworn. Odile recognizes her predecessor among them, still serving. Beat: seduction and revulsion entwined.

chapters.title: An Audience with Lady Sable
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Sable receives them courteously, offers Ines their forgotten memories back if they swear the court's counter-oath. She shows a glimpse: Ines was the one who brokered Veth's sale. Beat: the ground of self dissolving.

chapters.title: The Price of Remembering
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, reeling. Ines confronts what they might have done and cannot verify any of it — Sable controls all evidence. Wren insists the truth doesn't matter, only the choice ahead. Beat: despair met by a child's stubborn faith.

chapters.title: Cassian's Bargain
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Cassian formally switches sides, offering Sable's floor plans in exchange for nothing — he wants his name cleared by act, not contract. Odile distrusts him; Ines vouches. Beat: redemption chosen without guarantee.

chapters.title: The Soul Vault
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The infiltration reaches the vault where Veth's soul hangs in a lantern of oaths, each chain a promise made in the god's name. Ines touches it and hears every prayer ever answered. Beat: overwhelming intimacy with the divine.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile's old masters catch the group; offered reinstatement, she hesitates one fatal second and Cassian is captured. She chooses the rebels at last, burning the ward-lattice to cover their escape. Beat: hesitation, then costly commitment.

chapters.title: What Ines Sold
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, in Sable's custody briefly. Sable plays the full memory: Ines, desperate and dying, sold Veth's location to save their crew — and the god let itself be taken to spare them guilt. Beat: shame transfigured into understanding.

chapters.title: The New Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The sealing begins; the court's nobles converge, the exit roads close, and Wren begins to burn out holding the god's memory stable. Time collapses to hours. Beat: relentless acceleration.

chapters.title: Breaking the Oath
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines realizes every chain on the soul is an oath — including theirs. To free Veth they must renounce their loyalty, unmaking the identity they've built. They speak the renunciation as the vault shatters. Beat: sacrifice as liberation.

chapters.title: Veth Waking
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The soul pours home; Wren dissolves back into the god, who rises through the Undercourt unmaking Sable's stolen faces and offering even her mercy. The stars return one by one. Beat: terrible beauty, release.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Silence
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. The mountain stabilizes; the freed god does not restore the fallen or erase debts, only the leashes. Cassian buries his contract and walks out into starlight, owing nothing to anyone. Beat: quiet reckoning.

chapters.title: The Empty Brand
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines wakes with no memories before the mountain — the price of breaking the oath — and must decide who to be with a blank past and a scarred present. Odile stays; Cassian salutes and goes. Beat: grief accepted, identity rebuilt.

chapters.title: Roads Worth Walking
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, epilogue. Months later, Ines guides travelers through reopened Thornfell, teaching roads they're relearning from maps and kindness rather than compulsion. On the highest pass, a child's laugh sounds like an old friend. Beat: peace earned, forward-looking.
